issue.title: Plan propose to gate-shell handoff took 8m09s with zero phase timing telemetry
issue.description:
While diagnosing why agent sase-ws.3.f0's node showed DONE instead of TALE after a tale
plan proposal (2026-09-05), I found that the propose-to-gate-shell handoff took 8m09s
with no timing telemetry to explain where the time went.

Evidence (all on apollo, project gh_sase-org__sase, run 20260905064853):

- `agent_meta.json::plan_submitted_at` = 2026-09-05T11:08:10.185068+00:00 — recorded at
  the top of `handle_plan_marker` (src/sase/axe/run_agent_exec_plan.py:94), so the
  runner entered the plan-handoff path at 11:08:10 UTC.
- The plan gate's `request.json::created_at` = 2026-09-05T07:16:19.647788-04:00
  (11:16:19 UTC) and the gate member artifacts dir is stamped 20260905071619 — the gate
  shell materialized 8m09s later.
- The whole gap sits inside `_handle_plan_via_gate_shell` -> `create_plan_gate_shell`
  -> `create_gate_shell` (src/sase/plan_shell/create.py,
  src/sase/gate_shell/transaction.py). Nothing in that path logs phase timings, so the
  stall cannot be attributed post-hoc.
- One measured contributor: `list_gate_shells(project="gh_sase-org__sase")` (called by
  `_resolve_plan_shell_parent`, and again via `find_gate_shell_by_gate_id` /
  `has_any_gate_shell` inside the lane-locked transaction) took 9.18s to return 27
  records on a store whose TUI loader materializes 9,397 agent rows. Several such scans
  plus the lane lock could compound, but measured scans only account for tens of
  seconds — the dominant cost is unexplained.

Impact: during the propose-to-gate window the family has no gate row, so the review
request is invisible (compounded by the DONE-instead-of-TALE display defect, fixed
separately) and the user cannot approve the plan. An 8-minute invisible window per
proposal is a direct hit to the tale review loop.

Suggested first step: add phase-timing telemetry (spec build, parent resolution, lane
lock wait, member creation, claim move, gate creation) to the propose-to-gate path so
the next slow handoff is attributable, then optimize the dominant phase (likely the
repeated full gate-shell store scans).

task_type_fields.impact: Tale/epic review requests are invisible for the whole window (no gate row to approve), and there is no telemetry to attribute the stall.
task_type_fields.repro: Propose a tale plan via 'sase plan propose' on a project with a large agent-artifact store; compare agent_meta.json::plan_submitted_at with the gate request.json::created_at. Observed 8m09s on run 20260905064853; python -c timing of list_gate_shells(project=...) alone showed 9.18s per scan.

payload.description: The polyglot gate-command regression (broken approve scripts) came from the fix for sase-wt; both defects surfaced in the same 20260905064853 tale-proposal incident that exposed this latency
Both are gate-shell lifecycle observability gaps: sase-wp is silent follow-up launch failure, this is an unattributable propose-to-gate stall
